title: Pershing Square Sinks 12% on Second Downgrade in Two Days as BofA Cuts Target to $38
detail:
Pershing Square Sinks 12% on Second Downgrade in Two Days as BofA Cuts Target to $38
David Beren

BAC
PS
^GSPC
PSH.L
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Pershing Square Sinks 12% on Second Downgrade in Two Days as BofA Cuts Target to $38 ©mfto from Getty Images Signature, pixelshot via Canva
Key Takeaways

Pershing Square shares fell 12% after BofA downgraded the stock to Underperform and cut its price target to $38 from $54.

BofA lowered its 2026 to 2028 earnings estimates because of a delay in the PSV launch, and it now values the company more like other asset managers.

Citi's downgrade to Sell on Friday made the same point: earnings estimates have barely moved since the April IPO.

What to watch is the flagship fund's returns: Pershing Square Holdings' NAV fell 12.6% in the first half of 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 10.2%.

Pershing Square (PS:NYSE) sank 12% today after BofA downgraded Bill Ackman's asset manager to Underperform from Neutral before the open and cut its price target to $38 from $54.

It's the stock's second downgrade since Friday, when Citi cut it to Sell.

BofA stops paying up for growth

BofA lowered its 2026, 2027, and 2028 EPS estimates because the PSV launch has been delayed, and it also made a small change to its long-term return assumptions. It cut the multiple it uses too, to reflect a lower growth rate and to value Pershing Square the way it values the other asset managers it covers.

That second change matters more. Since its April IPO, the stock has traded as a growth story. BofA now prices it like its peers.

Citi made the same argument a few days earlier. In a note dated Oct. 9, it kept its $45 target and said the stock's rally had run ahead of its earnings outlook, with estimates broadly flat since the IPO because portfolio returns have been modest. The firm also cut its 2027 EPS estimate to $0.89 from $1.01.

The flagship fund has to deliver

Weak returns are behind both calls. The flagship Pershing Square Holdings (PSH) saw its NAV fall 12.6% in the first half of 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 10.2%. Lower returns mean fewer assets and smaller fees. Citi also now expects performance fees to come back later than it did before.

Even so, consensus still has earnings climbing steeply through 2028…

Pershing Square (PS): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2026–2028 (TIKR)

Those estimates are from Oct. 9, before BofA's cuts, and Citi's $0.89 for 2027 is already below the $0.96 consensus.

New funds carry the price

The growth story shows up in the multiple. Here's Pershing Square's forward P/E since it listed in April…

Pershing Square (PS): Normalized earnings P/E (TIKR)

Citi values the funds Pershing Square already runs at about $41 a share, and it adds $9 a share for future fund launches. A launch that slips hits the part of the value that hasn't arrived yet. BofA's $38 target is below Citi's value for the existing funds alone.

What would change the call

Back-to-back downgrades tell me Wall Street wants to see the new funds in action before it pays for them. Until PSV has a firm launch date and the flagship fund starts beating the market again, the stock will probably keep trading on the funds Pershing Square already runs.

title: McDonald's plans major store changes to attract more customers
detail:
McDonald's plans major store changes to attract more customers
Peace Longe
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 1:37 PM MDT 4 min read
MCD
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

McDonald's (MCD) operates about 13,800 restaurants across the United States, and the company just announced a plan to overhaul thousands of them.

On September 23, during its Investor Day, McDonald's detailed its broader growth strategy called McDonald's > NEXT. The strategy is built on four pillars:

Menu > NEXT (new food and drinks)

Consumer > NEXT (personalized marketing and loyalty)

Restaurant > NEXT (store remodels, simpler operations, and a generative AI system called ArchIQ)

People > NEXT (employee training and hospitality)

The pillar I'm particularly interested in is Restaurant > NEXT, as it involves a roughly $800,000-per-store remodeling plan.

Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski told investors the chain will rely on its "scale, customer insights, brand loyalty, and operational capabilities" to execute the plan. And Bank of America thinks it could be a step in the right direction.

BofA sees an $800,000 bet on remodeling with a four-year payback

According to a BofA Global Research note shared with me, analyst Sara Senatore expects McDonald's to spend about $800,000 on each traditional U.S. drive-thru to meet the Restaurant > NEXT standard. McDonald's expects franchisees to recoup their share of the investment in about four years, a payback period Senatore says "compares favorably" with previous remodelings.

Also read: McDonald's just did something not seen in decades

In the past, when McDonald's and rivals like Restaurant Brands International (QSR) and Wendy's (WEN) planned any upgrades, it often took about eight years or more to earn back the money they spent. A shorter payback period this time is one reason Senatore believes Restaurant > NEXT can improve the company's store-level sales.

But even though she believes the project can increase the company's sales, Senatore kept a Neutral rating on McDonald's and maintained her $343 price objective. She believes the long-term benefits are offset by how much the plan requires franchisees to spend and how long it takes for sales to increase.

Senatore is a Managing Director at Bank of America and has covered the restaurant group for nearly two decades, so many investors value her opinion.

McDonald's unveiled McDonald's > NEXT at its September 23, 2026 Investor Day in Chicago. BofA expects most Restaurant > NEXT remodels to begin in 2028, after key design and technology components come online.VV Shots / Getty Images
Why most of the remodels won't begin until 2028

Another thing to note is that very few remodels are expected to happen in 2027. In the BofA note I got, it was outlined that several design and technology pieces needed for Restaurant > NEXT won't be ready until 2028, which means most of the work won't start until then, or even 2029. BofA expects about 8,000 U.S. stores and 2,000 McDonald's stores in international operated markets to be remodeled across those two years.

title: Why Money Market Funds Are So Popular

Why Money Market Funds Are So Popular

Trading disclosure

US money market funds gathered more than $166 billion in the week ending October 7, 2026, according to Bank of America, marking their largest inflows since April 2020. Assets in money market funds have now topped $8 trillion, as these products remain popular with both institutional and retail investors due to their low risk and attractive short-term interest rates.

With the Federal Reserve expected to raise rates several times in the coming months, investors are preferring to stay at the shortest end of the yield curve and remain cautious about longer-duration bonds amid long-term inflation concerns. Even the Oracle of Omaha has accumulated a record amount of cash, most of which is invested in Treasury bills.

Investors should remember that as interest rates rise, bond prices fall, unless they invest in individual bonds and hold them to maturity. A recent Wall Street Journal survey indicated that economists expect interest rates to remain elevated for an extended period.

While stock-bond correlations have risen sharply over the past few years, cash and ultra-short-term bonds maintain virtually zero correlation with equities, offering meaningful diversification benefits to a portfolio.

Money Market ETFs: What Investors Should Know

This ETF category has attracted significant interest since Texas Capital launched the first money market ETF. Lower expense ratios compared with mutual funds and investors' preference for the ETF structure have helped drive demand. BlackRock, JPMorgan, and other providers have followed with their own money market ETFs.

Most money market mutual funds are required to maintain a net asset value (NAV) of $1 per share. Although their share prices do not appreciate, investors receive regular dividends, allowing their investments to grow over time.

Unlike traditional money market mutual funds, money market ETFs typically have fluctuating share prices and often launch with a NAV of around $100. Their NAVs may fluctuate slightly due to market demand, bid-ask spreads, and changes in underlying yields, but they generally remain close to their initial NAVs.

Government money market funds invest in Treasury bills and government agency securities, including those issued by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Prime money market funds invest in a mix of corporate and government securities.

Municipal money market funds are particularly appealing to high-income investors because the interest earned is generally exempt from federal income tax and may also be exempt from state income tax.

The index starts with the 500 largest U.S.-listed companies and keeps the 100 with the most analyst Buy recommendations, based on TipRanks' data. It then looks at price momentum, meaning how each stock's recent price compares with its longer-term averages, and selects the 50 stocks with the strongest momentum. Holdings are weighted by market capitalization, subject to caps at the company and sector level, and the index is reconstituted quarterly.
